speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience pain in the leg, and does elevating it provide relief? I would also like to see the wound to assess for signs of venous stasis or arterial insufficiency. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the wound have a shallow, irregular border with yellowish exudate, and do you notice brownish discoloration or hardening of the skin around the ankle? I will also check for the presence of a palpable pulse in your foot.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Deep vein thrombosis in the right leg 5 years prior. No other significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works as an accountant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the wound produce a moderate amount of serous or serosanguineous drainage, and is the surrounding skin indurated and hyperpigmented? I will now check for a palpable pedal pulse and assess for pitting edema.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, recent injuries, heart disease, or diabetes.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of DVT, chronic swelling, and family history, this presentation is highly suggestive of venous stasis. I will now confirm the physical signs of venous insufficiency. REQUEST TEST: Venous_Duplex_Ultrasound
